boundary_decision.status: accepted as a learner education, award and recognition context
boundary_decision.rationale: The model joins learner-programme participation and assessed outcomes to a personal qualification award, credential evidence and later recognition decisions. It keeps people, institutions, programmes, teaching, assessments, skills, occupations, licences, consent and proof infrastructure in their own masters.

decisions.rationale: Participation, attendance, component completion, assessed achievement, qualification definition, personal award, credential, recognition and authorization cannot be inferred from one another.

decisions.disposition: accepted as separately mastered reusable definitions
decisions.rationale: A programme defines a learning route and rules, while a qualification defines a reusable outcome; each has its own identifier, owner, version and jurisdiction.

decisions.disposition: accepted as the person-specific qualification fact
decisions.rationale: The competent awarding decision and effective conferral create the personal award, which remains distinct from both source learning evidence and issued credentials.

decisions.disposition: accepted as evidence with independent status
decisions.rationale: A credential asserts an award or achievement but its issue, reissue, suspension and revocation lifecycle can diverge from the underlying learning and award history.
ISCED supports programme and related-qualification classification and national mappings but does not accredit a provider, validate learning or confer an award.
EQF and national framework mappings express attributable comparison of learning outcomes and never prove automatic qualification equivalence or recognition.
Every mapped value retains the source scale, system, version, authority and transformation because grades, credit and workload are jurisdiction and institution specific.

decisions.disposition: accepted as external execution plus local effect
decisions.rationale: Assessment instruments and attempts retain external masters while this model stores source results, scales, moderation, appeal and their validated effect on outcomes or award eligibility.
A recognizing authority decides comparability or acceptance for one purpose and jurisdiction; the decision never mutates the source qualification or grants a professional licence automatically.
CLR, Open Badges and Verifiable Credentials carry selected claims and evidence but do not replace registrar or awarding-body masters and must preserve disclosure and status limits.

decisions.disposition: accepted with minimum disclosure and sealed-record controls
decisions.rationale: Public verification must expose only the required claim and cannot reveal the complete transcript, unrelated achievements, internal identifiers or protected records.
